_comment: The indexing engine release Shimmr bundles.
These point at the ENGINE PROJECT'S OWN published release artifacts, never
at a binary we built. A build we produce has a different build fingerprint,
and the engine refuses to run two differing builds for one OS account
(ADR 0007) — a self-built bundle would fail to start for any customer who
already runs the engine directly.
Linux uses the -portable asset: the engine's own build script documents
STATIC=1 as a 'fully static portable build (Alpine/musl leg)', and its own
installer resolves the portable asset on Linux. A static binary is what
survives being installed across arbitrary distributions.
macOS and Windows publish no portable variant, so the plain asset is the
only one. The '-ui-' assets are byte-identical aliases of these, not
separate builds — same checksums.
Checksums are as published by GitHub on the release assets.
tool_count is what this release's binary exposes through tools/list. The
release job asserts it against the real binary, so a bump that changes the
surface fails the release rather than reaching a customer who counts.
release_commit is the commit the release was cut from. It is NOT the commit
we first read the source at: that one is 246 commits later, and it has two
tools this release does not. Read the release, not main — see section 2 of
docs/01-engine-findings.md.
Bumping the engine is deliberate: update version, update release_commit,
update every sha256, re-check the tool count against the new binary, and
note it in docs/internal/ATTRIBUTION.md.
